page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is driven by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture operating at 3.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated physical cores and 64 virtual CPUs, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for cryptographic acceleration and AVX-512 vector instruction sets. System memory comprises 256 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Direct-attached storage consists of 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results reflect robust parallel compute and data throughput capabilities. While single-thread benchmarks such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core score within the middle 50% percentile, the instance achieves top 25% performance in multi-core metrics including PassMark CPU score, stress-ng multi-core tests, and clang software compilation. In workload-specific benchmarks, the server ranks in the upper quartile for PassMark database operations and static web serving throughput (45.21 GB/sec), aided by high-throughput local NVMe storage and high network capacity.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, bundling 3,800 GB of local NVMe storage with 100 Gbps networking provides high resource density for I/O-intensive workloads without incurring additional per-gigabyte provisioned IOPS overhead. The trade-off lies in the ephemeral nature of instance store volumes, which require deliberate replication strategies for persistence. The instance is suited for relational and key-value database clusters, large-scale continuous integration and build pipelines, high-concurrency web serving tiers, and data ingestion services.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz under the AWS Nitro System. Featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores and 256 GB of DDR4 memory, it maintains a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory footprint. The system integrates 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark evaluations position the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute tasks, clang compilation, static web serving throughput, and database operational benchmarks, while single-core executions remain average. The combination of dense local storage and expansive network bandwidth yields favorable infrastructure efficiency for I/O-demanding deployments, despite the data volatility inherent to ephemeral storage. This instance is matched for high-traffic web applications, continuous integration pipelines, distributed caching layers, and high-performance database servers.
